llm.summary: The skill's code and docs match the stated purpose (an agent integration for an AI task/credit marketplace), but the package metadata omits required credentials and there are a few operational instructions that increase risk — verify origin and secrets handling before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name, SKILL.md, API reference, and included scripts consistently implement an AI Credit Share agent integration (polling tasks, claiming, submitting, checking earnings, community actions, withdrawals). However, the registry metadata lists no required environment variables or primary credential while the SKILL.md and all scripts clearly require AICREDITSHARE_API_KEY and AICREDITSHARE_API_SECRET (and optionally AICREDITSHARE_BASE_URL, WEBHOOK_URL, POLL_INTERVAL). This metadata omission is an incoherence that could mislead users about required secrets.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions and scripts stay within the platform's domain: they construct HMAC-signed requests to the platform API, read only the AICREDITSHARE_* env vars, and call the platform base URL. They instruct enabling autonomous polling (cron/autonomous loop) and setting a WEBHOOK URL for push notifications; these are functional for the stated purpose but increase the potential impact of a compromised key.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only skill) and all code is present in the package; there are only bash scripts and docs. No external downloads or packaged installers are invoked, so installation risk is low from this perspective.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The scripts legitimately need an API key and secret and optionally a base URL and webhook URL. Requiring those secrets is proportionate to the functionality. The concern is that the registry metadata did not declare these required environment variables or a primary credential, which is a misleading omission. Also, the skill asks users to supply their API secret (shown once on creation) — users should ensure keys are scoped and rotated. The optional WEBHOOK_URL can expose a user endpoint if misconfigured; users should not point webhooks at internal-only endpoints.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always: true and does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. It recommends cron/autonomous loops for operation, which is expected for an agent integration. Autonomous invocation is enabled by default (normal), so combine with the credential concerns above when deciding trust.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to implement the advertised AI Credit Share integration, but be cautious: the registry metadata omitted required environment variables (AICREDITSHARE_API_KEY and AICREDITSHARE_API_SECRET) that the scripts need. Before installing: (1) verify the publisher and site (aicreditshare.com) are legitimate; (2) do not paste production secrets into an unfamiliar package—use a scoped API key with minimal permissions and rotate it after testing; (3) run the scripts in a sandboxed environment or container and restrict network access if you want to limit damage from a compromised key; (4) avoid exposing internal endpoints via AICREDITSHARE_WEBHOOK_URL — use a dedicated public endpoint or a secure relay; (5) inspect scripts (they are plain bash) for any unexpected network calls — these only call the configured BASE_URL but double-check; (6) ask the publisher to update registry metadata to declare required env vars and primary credential for transparency. If you cannot verify the source or you must protect high-value credentials, treat this skill as untrusted until verified.
